title: Your First 5 AI Prompts to Save Time Every Day
style: Read this like a friendly, confident teacher explaining to a small business owner. Warm, clear, unhurried, natural pauses.

segments.title: 5 prompts that save you time every day
segments.say: What if five simple prompts could give you back thirty minutes or more, every single day? In this video, I'll give you five copy-and-paste prompts for your email, your day, your paperwork, your marketing and your decisions. They work in Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini, and every one of them is in the description. If you're new here, hit subscribe, because every week we make AI simple, one step at a time.

segments.title: How to use these prompts
bullets: Copy the prompt from the description
Replace anything in [BRACKETS] with your details
Never paste passwords, card numbers or private customer data
Talk back: "shorter", "friendlier", "what did I miss?"
segments.say: Quick setup. Copy each prompt from the description. Anything in square brackets, you replace with your own details. Keep it safe: never paste passwords, card numbers or private customer information. And remember from our first video: don't stop at the first answer. Talk back. Say, make it shorter, make it friendlier, or, what did I miss?

segments.title: Reply to any email in seconds
bullets: Paste the email you received
Say what you want to happen
Set the tone and the length
segments.say: Prompt one: reply to any email. Paste in the email you got, then say: write a reply that, and what you want to happen. Then the tone and the length. For example, a customer wants to return a table after thirty days. Your policy says no, but you want to keep them happy. In seconds you get a kind, clear reply that offers store credit instead. You just edit and send.

chat.user: Here's an email I got: [paste]. Write a reply that says we can't refund after 30 days, but offer store credit. Kind and clear, under 80 words.
chat.ai: Hi Maria, thank you for reaching out, and I'm sorry the table isn't working out. Our refund window is 30 days, so we can't issue a refund, but we'd be happy to give you full store credit for the table. Just stop by any time. — Dana

segments.title: Plan your day in one minute
bullets: List everything on your plate
Tell it how many hours you have
Ask for an order and time blocks
segments.say: Prompt two: plan your day. Dump everything on your plate into the chat, messy is fine. Tell it how many hours you have. Then ask it to put the tasks in order, most important first, with time blocks. It's like having a calm assistant who turns your to-do pile into a real plan, and tells you what can wait until tomorrow.

chat.user: My tasks today: [call supplier, post sale on Facebook, pay invoices, train new hire, reorder mattresses]. I have 6 hours. Order them, most important first, with time blocks.
chat.ai:
9:00 Pay invoices (30 min)
9:30 Call supplier + reorder mattresses (45 min)
10:15 Train new hire (2 hrs)
12:15 Lunch
1:00 Post the sale on Facebook (30 min)
Can wait: deep-cleaning the stockroom.

segments.title: Summarize anything long
bullets: Paste text or upload a PDF or photo
Ask for 5 bullet points
Ask for action items and deadlines
segments.say: Prompt three: summarize anything long. A contract, a supplier update, a long email thread, a policy. Paste it in or upload the file, and ask for a summary in five bullet points, plus every action item and deadline. Reading a twenty-page document now takes two minutes. Just remember to double check the important numbers yourself.

chat.user: [supplier_terms.pdf] Summarize this in 5 bullet points. Then list every action item and deadline.
chat.ai:
• Prices go up 4% on Jan 1
• Free shipping now starts at $1,500
• Returns need approval within 14 days
• Net-30 payment terms stay the same
• New online ordering portal
Action items: place holiday orders before Dec 10 to lock in current prices.

segments.title: Write a week of posts
bullets: Say what you sell and who buys it
Give the offer or news
Ask for 3 versions to choose from
segments.say: Prompt four: marketing. Tell it what you sell, who your customers are, and what you want to promote. Then ask for three short posts to choose from, friendly, with a question at the end to get comments. Pick the one you like, ask for small changes, and post it. That's a week of social media in about ten minutes.

chat.user: I run a [furniture store]. Write 3 short Facebook posts about our [weekend recliner sale, 20% off]. Friendly, one emoji max, end with a question.
chat.ai:
1) Sunday naps just got an upgrade. All recliners are 20% off this weekend only! Which color would you pick? 🛋️
2) ...
3) ...

segments.title: Make better decisions
bullets: Describe the two options
Ask it to ask YOU questions first
Then get pros, cons and a recommendation
segments.say: Prompt five is my favorite: make better decisions. Describe the choice you're stuck on. Then add this magic line: ask me three questions first, before you answer. Now it understands your situation, and gives you pros, cons and a recommendation that actually fits you. Use it for hiring, buying, pricing, or even which phone plan to pick. You still make the final call.

chat.user: I'm deciding between [hiring a part-time helper] and [paying for a delivery service]. Ask me 3 questions first, then give pros, cons and a recommendation.
chat.ai:
Happy to help! First:
1. How many deliveries do you do per week?
2. What's your monthly budget for this?
3. Would a helper also cover the store floor?

segments.title: Keep your favorite prompts handy
bullets: Save them in a note on your phone
Make a version for each repeat task
Reuse the same chat for the same job
segments.say: A quick tip to save even more time. Save your favorite prompts in a note on your phone, with the brackets ready to fill. Make one version for each task you repeat every week. And when you come back to the same job, like weekly posts, continue in the same chat, so the AI already knows your store and your style.

segments.title: How much time could this save?
bullets: Email replies: about 10 minutes a day
Planning your day: about 10 minutes
Reading and summarizing: about 10 minutes
Your results will vary. Track it for one week
segments.say: Let's do some rough math. If these prompts save you around ten minutes on email, ten on planning, and ten on reading, that's half an hour a day, or about two and a half hours in a work week. These are estimates, and your results will be different. So track it yourself for one week, and tell me in the comments what you saved.

segments.title: Try one prompt a day this week
bullets: Mon: Reply to an email
Tue: Plan your day
Wed: Summarize a document
Thu: Write a post
Fri: Make a decision
segments.say: Here's your challenge. One prompt a day, this week. Monday: reply to an email. Tuesday: plan your day. Wednesday: summarize a document. Thursday: write a social post. Friday: make a decision with the ask me questions first trick. Comment which prompt helped you most. I read every comment.
